entities.name: Semeon Olshanski
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Semeon Yurievich Olshanski (died March 13, 1505) was a pivotal magnate and statesman of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, whose career as Castellan of Vilnius and Palatine of Polotsk profoundly influenced the political landscape of the late 15th century. As a scion of the powerful Olshanski noble family, he navigated the complex dynastic politics of the Jagiellonian era, playing a crucial role in the state's internal administration and its external relations with Muscovy and the Crimean Khanate. His influence stemmed not only from his high offices but also from the extensive landholdings and military retainers commanded by his lineage, making him a key player in the Council of Lords that advised the Grand Duke.

Olshanski's public service began with his appointment as Palatine of Polotsk in 1482, a strategic frontier region, where he was responsible for defense and local governance. His most significant ascent occurred in 1492 when he became Castellan of Vilnius, the highest non-ducal office in the Grand Duchy. In this capacity, he presided over the Vilnius Sejm and served as a leading member of the Council of Lords, effectively acting as a co-ruler alongside Grand Duke Alexander Jagiellon. He was instrumental in shaping the Grand Duchy's response to the escalating Muscovite-Lithuanian Wars, particularly after the Battle of Vedrosha in 1500, and participated in diplomatic efforts to secure alliances. His wealth and prestige were further cemented through strategic marriages and land acquisitions, expanding the Olshanski family's already vast domains.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Semeon Olshanski was a leading magnate whose high offices and political influence helped shape the Grand Duchy of Lithuania's internal governance and foreign policy during a critical period of conflict with Muscovy, contributing to the evolution of the magnate class's power.
